# #4363: Patch: the music player's background prefetch waits while the browser asks to save data, as the voice prefetch already does
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A player on a metered connection who asked their browser to save data still gets the game's music downloaded in the background once a match starts: the danger track, the result stings and every card intro in their hand. The voice lines already wait in that case; the music does not, so the same Save-Data player can silently spend mobile data on music while the voices stay quiet.

## Why

Issue #4329 (R4316000) gated the voice prefetch behind the Save-Data signal: `apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts` checks `savingData()` before fetching voice bytes in the background, and `apps/web/src/net/saveData.ts` documents the signal as shared. The music player never reads it. `apps/web/src/audio/musicDirector.ts` asks for the danger track, the result tracks and each hand card's intro (`preloadHand`, called from `settle()`, plus `sink.preload` on the first view and on station switches), and `apps/web/src/audio/music.ts` `pumpPreload()` fetches those bytes whenever the player is idle and the music or stings are audible (`audible()`/`stingAudible()` only look at the volume settings). The assets are large: `apps/web/public/audio/music` is about 51 MB (the voice folder about 21 MB), a single danger track is ~1.2 MB (`tavern-danger` `bytes: 1263040` in `music-manifest.json`), and a ten-card hand can queue ten more intro fetches. A Save-Data player with the sound on therefore downloads megabytes of music in the background of every game while the 20 MB of voice lines correctly wait.

## Proposal

Thread the existing `savingData()` signal into the music player's background fetching, mirroring the voice prefetch: `pumpPreload()` (and the `fetchCached`/`fetchIntro` paths it drives) does nothing while `savingData()` is true, so held preloads stay held instead of downloaded. Keep every on-demand fetch working: the track the player actually needs now (`sync()`/`decode` for playback, `playIntro`/`playSting` for a card just played) still downloads, exactly as a voice line still plays on demand while its prefetch waits. When the signal clears, the held preloads drain as they do today. No settings UI changes and no manifest changes.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/audio/music.ts` (`pumpPreload`, `fetchCached`, `fetchIntro`)
- `apps/web/src/audio/musicDirector.ts` (preload call sites stay as-is; the sink holds)
- `apps/web/src/net/saveData.ts` (already the shared signal, R2116000)
- SPEC §10.11 (sound) needs no change; the voice precedent is R4316000

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `saveData: true`, a game view downloads no music bytes in the background (danger/result/intro fetches), while the current track and played-card stings still download and play
- [ ] With `saveData: false`, prefetch behavior is byte-for-byte what it is today
- [ ] `music.test.ts`/`musicDirector.test.ts` gain cases for the held-while-saving and drain-after-clearing behavior that fail without the gate
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test <touched files>` passes; no new network requests appear in the Save-Data path

## Size and risks

Small: one gate plus tests. Risk is under-prefetching (a sting arrives late on a Save-Data connection that just cleared); mitigated because playback fetches are untouched and the held queue drains on the next idle pump.
